findings.title: Minimum token schema is malformed and strips required token fields
findings.body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create wildcard/dynamic Zod keys; they create literal '[object Object]'-style keys, one of which is a required number. Responses containing only access_token/expiry from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT therefore fail safeParse and throw 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', while Zod's default stripping also drops fields such as refresh_token, expiry_date/expires_in, scope and provider-specific fields that callers persist. Credential-sync refresh is effectively broken for Google, Office365, Zoom and Salesforce.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token'
findings.body: When the sync endpoint correctly returns only an access token, this code invents refresh_token='refresh_token' instead of preserving the stored refresh token. Callers such as Zoom (key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token), Office365 (spreading tokenResponse.data over stored credentials) and Google then persist that placeholder, destroying the real refresh token so the next refresh fails with invalid_grant and the credential becomes unusable.

findings.title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response incompatible with most callers
findings.body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response, but callers were written for incompatible return types: HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object (accessToken/expiresIn become undefined), ZohoCRM/Zoho-Bigin expect an Axios response with .data (tokenInfo.data is undefined on a Response and .error access crashes/misbehaves), and Google expects res.data (token.access_token throws). Only fetch-based callers expecting a Response can work, so enabling sync breaks refresh for several apps. It also never checks response.ok or parses JSON, so HTTP errors from the sync endpoint are treated as successful token responses.

findings.title: SafeParse result object is persisted as the credential key
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), but this code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); prisma.credential.update({data:{key}})`, whereas previously googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the token data itself. The stored key becomes {success:true, data:{...}}, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on the next use fails/missing access_token and refresh_token, corrupting the Google credential even without credential sync enabled.

findings.title: New Salesforce refresh code uses unimported prisma and discards the refreshed token
findings.body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update but prisma is never imported in this file, causing a TypeScript/ReferenceError on every Salesforce client creation. Even if it ran, the jsforce Connection at lines 101-108 is built with credentialKey.access_token (the old, expired token) instead of accessTokenParsed.data.access_token, so the freshly fetched and persisted token is never used.

findings.title: Credential ID is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects a user ID
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens' third argument is userId and is sent to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId (the credential primary key) instead of credential.userId. With sync enabled the parent platform will look up/refresh tokens for the wrong user (or no user), returning wrong credentials or failing refresh. The service does not retain credential.userId in biginAuth, only credential.id.

findings.title: Webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time equality and handler has no error handling
findings.body: The shared secret used to authorize writing arbitrary user credentials is compared with !==, allowing timing-based secret recovery, instead of a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual with length checks). Additionally the handler imposes no HTTP-method check and lets z.object.parse (line 31), symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse (lines 57-59) throw uncaught, turning malformed/unauthenticated-shape payloads into 500s rather than controlled 400 responses.
